The Lord comes down from his holy place. What does God's coming mean for the earth?
Micah lamented over his people's wound. How can you grieve for those who are hurting?
Woe to those who plan evil on their beds. How do our plans reveal our hearts?
God will gather his people like sheep and the breaker will go up before them. How does Jesus lead his flock?
Micah was "filled with power, with the Spirit of the Lord, and with justice and might." How does God's Spirit empower you to speak truth?
Leaders judged for a bribe and still said, "Is not the Lord in the midst of us?" How can we fool ourselves about God's presence?
Nations will stream to the Lord's mountain and beat swords into ploughshares. What does this vision of peace stir in you?
"They shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree, and no one shall make them afraid." What does God's peace look like?
A ruler will come from Bethlehem, "whose coming forth is from of old." How does this point to Jesus?
"He shall stand and shepherd his flock in the strength of the Lord... And he shall be their peace." How is Jesus your peace?
God asked, "O my people, what have I done to you?" How does God's faithfulness call us back?
"What does the Lord require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?" Which do you need to grow in?
"I will look to the Lord; I will wait for the God of my salvation; my God will hear me." How do you wait for God?
"When I fall, I shall rise; when I sit in darkness, the Lord will be a light to me." Where do you need this hope?
"Who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity... You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea." What does God's pardon mean to you?
